title: Terms & Conditions
content:
Last updated: 03/08/2026

These Terms and Conditions apply to software development, Python/Django consultancy and related technical services provided by Stockgrove Brickhill Systems Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales under company number 06438539, whose registered office is 'The Barn' Pear Tree Lane, Whitchurch, Shropshire SY13 1NG ("the Company", "we", "us" or "our").

They apply to services supplied to business customers ("the Client", "you" or "your").

By accepting a quotation, proposal or statement of work from us, you agree to these Terms and Conditions.

1. Services

We provide software development and technical consultancy services, including Python and Django development, web application development, software maintenance, troubleshooting, code review, database development, automation and related services.

The specific services, deliverables and requirements for each project will be set out in our quotation, proposal or statement of work ("the Project Specification").

2. Fixed-price projects

Projects are undertaken for the fixed fee stated in the agreed Project Specification.

The fixed fee applies only to the work and requirements described in the Project Specification. Requests for additional functionality, changes to requirements or work outside the agreed scope may result in additional charges.

Where additional work is requested, we will normally agree the additional cost and any impact on the delivery schedule with you before undertaking that work.

3. Project requirements and changes

You agree to provide information, access, materials, technical requirements and decisions reasonably necessary for us to complete the project.

If requirements change after the Project Specification has been agreed, we may revise the project price and delivery schedule to reflect the additional work.

Changes may include, for example:

  • additional features;

  • changes to agreed functionality;

  • integration with additional systems;

  • changes to third-party services;

  • changes to design or technical requirements; or

  • work resulting from information or requirements that were not available when the project was specified.

4. Fees and payment

The project fee will be stated in the applicable quotation, proposal or Project Specification.

Unless otherwise agreed, invoices are payable within 30 days of the invoice date.

We may require a deposit or staged payments for larger projects. Any such payment schedule will be specified in the Project Specification.

All prices are exclusive of VAT unless expressly stated otherwise. VAT will be charged where applicable.

If an invoice remains unpaid after its due date, we may suspend work on the project until payment is received.

We reserve the right to charge interest and compensation on overdue commercial debts in accordance with the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998, where applicable.

5. Delivery

We will use reasonable endeavours to complete the project by the estimated delivery date stated in the Project Specification.

Delivery dates may be affected by:

  • changes to requirements;

  • delays in receiving information or approvals from you;

  • delays caused by third-party suppliers or services;

  • technical issues outside our reasonable control; or

  • other circumstances beyond our reasonable control.

Where such circumstances occur, we will discuss any material impact on the delivery schedule with you.

6. Acceptance

The deliverables will be considered accepted when they materially conform to the requirements set out in the Project Specification.

You should notify us of any material defect or failure to meet the agreed specification within a reasonable period after delivery.

We will use reasonable efforts to correct defects that result in the deliverables materially failing to meet the agreed specification.

Acceptance does not include changes to requirements or requests for functionality that was not included in the original Project Specification.

7. Intellectual property

Unless otherwise agreed in writing, ownership of bespoke source code and other deliverables specifically created for the Client as part of a project will transfer to the Client once all invoices relating to that project have been paid in full.

We retain ownership of any pre-existing intellectual property, software, libraries, frameworks, templates, tools, utilities, techniques, processes and know-how that we use or incorporate into a project.

Where pre-existing intellectual property is incorporated into a deliverable, we grant the Client a non-exclusive licence to use that intellectual property as reasonably necessary to use the deliverables.

Third-party and open-source software remains subject to its applicable licence terms.

We retain the right to use general skills, knowledge, experience, techniques and know-how acquired while carrying out a project, provided that doing so does not disclose the Client's confidential information or infringe the Client's intellectual property.

8. Client materials

You retain ownership of software, data, content, images, documentation and other materials supplied to us.

You confirm that you have the necessary rights and permissions for us to use those materials in providing the services.

You grant us a limited right to use such materials solely for the purposes of completing the agreed project.

9. Confidentiality

Each party agrees to keep confidential information received from the other party confidential and not to disclose it to third parties except:

  • with the other party's permission;

  • where disclosure is necessary to provide the services;

  • to professional advisers who are subject to confidentiality obligations; or

  • where disclosure is required by law.

These confidentiality obligations do not apply to information that is already publicly available through no breach of these Terms, was lawfully known before disclosure, or is independently developed without using confidential information.

10. Data protection

Each party will comply with applicable UK data protection legislation.

Where we process personal data on your behalf as a data processor, the parties will enter into any additional data processing agreement or arrangements required by applicable law.

You are responsible for ensuring that any personal data supplied to us may lawfully be processed for the purposes of the project.

11. Security and access

Where you provide access to hosting accounts, repositories, databases, APIs or other systems, you are responsible for providing appropriate access and permissions.

We will take reasonable steps to protect credentials and access information provided to us.

Unless expressly agreed otherwise, you remain responsible for the security and operation of your production systems after delivery.

12. Backups

Unless specifically included in the Project Specification, maintaining backups of your production systems, databases, files and other data is your responsibility.

We will take reasonable care when working with your systems but cannot guarantee that data will never be lost or corrupted.

13. Third-party services

Projects may depend upon third-party services, hosting providers, APIs, software libraries or other infrastructure.

We are not responsible for the availability, performance, security, pricing or continued operation of third-party services that are outside our control.

Where a project depends materially upon a third-party service, this will be identified where reasonably practicable.

14. Warranties

We warrant that the services will be performed with reasonable care and skill.

Unless expressly stated otherwise, we do not warrant that software will be completely free from defects or that it will operate without interruption.

Any specific warranty relating to a project must be set out in the applicable Project Specification.

15. Liability

Nothing in these Terms limits or excludes liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or any other liability that cannot legally be limited or excluded.

Subject to the above, neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of anticipated savings, loss of business or loss of opportunity arising from the project.

Our total aggregate liability arising from or in connection with a project shall not exceed the total fees actually paid or payable to us under that project.

This limitation does not apply to liabilities that cannot legally be limited or excluded.

16. Termination

Either party may terminate a project if the other party commits a material breach of these Terms and fails to remedy that breach within a reasonable period after receiving written notice.

We may suspend or terminate work where invoices remain substantially overdue.

If a project is terminated, the Client remains responsible for payment for work completed and approved expenses incurred up to the termination date.

Where appropriate, we will provide the Client with completed work and materials for which payment has been received.

17. Force majeure

Neither party shall be responsible for failure or delay in performing its obligations where that failure or delay results from circumstances beyond its reasonable control.

This may include significant technical failures, interruption of essential services, natural disasters, serious illness, industrial disputes, government action or changes in law.

The affected party will take reasonable steps to minimise the effects of such circumstances.

18. Subcontractors

We may use suitably qualified subcontractors or third-party suppliers to assist with delivery of a project where reasonably necessary.

We remain responsible for the services provided by subcontractors engaged by us.

We will ensure that subcontractors who have access to confidential information are subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.

19. Publicity

We will not publicly identify the Client or use the Client's name, logo or project details for marketing purposes without the Client's prior consent.

Unless otherwise agreed, we may refer generally to the skills and technologies used in a project without disclosing confidential information.

20. Entire agreement

The agreed Project Specification, quotation or proposal together with these Terms and Conditions constitute the agreement between the parties relating to the relevant project.

If there is a conflict between these Terms and Conditions and an expressly agreed Project Specification, the Project Specification will take precedence for matters specific to that project.

21. Changes to these Terms

These Terms and Conditions may be updated from time to time.

The version applicable to a particular project will normally be the version agreed when the project is accepted, unless the parties subsequently agree otherwise in writing.

22. Governing law and jurisdiction

These Terms and Conditions and any dispute or claim arising from them shall be governed by the laws of England and Wales.

The courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes arising from or in connection with these Terms and Conditions, subject to any agreement between the parties to resolve a dispute by another method.
